newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-DAVENPORT AND RAYMOND REACH IGA CLASSIC FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DAVENPORT AND RAYMOND REACH IGA CLASSIC FINAL.

text.p: Top seed Lindsay Davenport shook off a slow start, while Lisa Raymond won in a breeze on Saturday to advance to the finals of the $164,250 IGA Tennis Classic.
Davenport gained a measure of revenge with a 1-6 6-2 6-3 victory over third-seeded Kimberly Po, who eliminated the Olympic champion at last month's Australian Open.
The fourth-seeded Raymond rocked unseeded Francesca Lubiana of Italy 6-1 6-0 in a 41-minute mismatch.
Davenport will try to extend her unbeaten streak against Raymond in Sunday's final. She is 3-0 against fellow-American Raymond including a 6-3 6-4 win last month in the Sydney International.

Lubiani knocked off sixth-seeded Amy Frazier in the first round and then shocked second seed Amanda Coetzer 6-0 6-4 in Friday's semifinals. But the 19-year-old Italian ran out of magic against Raymond, 26th in the tour rankings.
Lubiana, ranked 110th, won only the fourth game in the first set. "I never let her in the match," Raymond said. "I played pretty well flawless tennis and never allowed her to play her game."
Po needed just 19 minutes to take the first set against Davenport.
But Davenport, ranked eighth in the world, took control in the second set with three service breaks.
Both players held serve in the third set as Davenport led 4-3. She broke serve in the eighth game then held serve again for the 6-3 win.
The 19th-ranked Po had two victories in four previous matches against Davenport.
"She started off really, really well," Davenport said of her long-time rival and fellow-Californian. "She played some of the best tennis anyone has ever played against me.
"There wasn't much I could do. I just hung in there and wasn't down on myself."
Davenport said her showing here had helped her get over disappointing results in Australia last month.
"I didn't play well in Australia, so it feels good to be winning again," she said. "Winning is a good way to get your confidence back."
Davenport lost to Jennifer Capriati in the semifinals of the Sydney International before losing to Po in the fourth round of the Australian Open.
She avenged both those losses here, beating Capriati in straight sets in the quarter-finals.
